nodes.name: Phytoplankton
nodes.desc: Microscopic drifting algae that feed the whole open lake. Invasive mussels now filter much of this food from the water.

nodes.name: Zooplankton
nodes.desc: Tiny animals that graze algae. Alewife and juvenile fish eat them, and so do filtering mussels.

nodes.name: Mysis
nodes.desc: A native shrimp-like crustacean of cold deep water. It eats mainly zooplankton, or algae and detritus when zooplankton is scarce.

nodes.name: Diporeia
nodes.desc: A native lake-bottom amphipod that fell sharply from the 1990s, which invasive mussels are thought to have caused.

nodes.name: Quagga & zebra mussels
nodes.desc: Invasive filter feeders that strip plankton from the water and clear it. They are now the main drain on the lake's food supply.

nodes.name: Alewife
nodes.desc: An invasive herring that eats zooplankton. It became the main prey for stocked salmon and trout.

nodes.name: Lake whitefish
nodes.desc: Young fish eat plankton and larger ones eat bottom animals like snails and mussels. Its condition fell as Diporeia declined.

nodes.name: Sea lamprey
nodes.desc: An invasive parasite that feeds on the blood of large fish such as lake trout and whitefish. It is held in check by control programs.

nodes.name: Double-crested cormorant
nodes.desc: A diving fish-eating bird. Alewife is believed to have created good feeding conditions for Great Lakes colonies.

nodes.name: Herring gull
nodes.desc: A scavenging shore bird that picks up dead fish, including alewife die-offs, from the beach.

nodes.name: Lake trout
nodes.desc: The native top predator, nearly wiped out by lampreys and overfishing. Hatchery stocking helps rebuild it.

nodes.name: Chinook salmon
nodes.desc: Stocked since 1967 to control alewife. Adults eat mostly fish, and the population depends on yearly stocking.

nodes.name: Bald eagle
nodes.desc: A fish-eating raptor of the lakeshore that takes live and dead fish.

nodes.name: Sunlight
nodes.desc: Sunlight reaches algae in the upper lake. Clearer water lets light go deeper.

nodes.name: Phosphorus
nodes.desc: The nutrient that limits algae growth in the open lake. Mussels hold much of it near the shore and bottom.

nodes.name: Cold deep water
nodes.desc: Cold bottom water below the thermocline is the home of Mysis, Diporeia and lake trout.

nodes.name: Decomposers
nodes.desc: Break down dead algae, fish and mussels and return phosphorus to the water.
